AI structure auditing / current record

Recovery can be real.
Composition can still fail.

The latest VARZIN experiments separate five questions that older site summaries sometimes compressed: surface clustering, frozen representation content, trained remediation, true algebraic-position recovery, and systematic composition on unseen combinations.

Frozen baselinesExplicit interventionHeld-out composition
Current conclusion

The strongest current evidence is not “models recover LUXVAR meaning” and not “models contain no structure.” It is narrower: targeted structural information can be strongly recoverable or decodable under specified procedures, while the tested systematic-composition criteria remain unmet.

01 / evidence ladder

Five questions that must remain separate.

1

Surface / morphology

What regularities are already present in the constructed strings, roots, prefixes and tokenization?

2

Frozen representation

Can a target variable be decoded from an unmodified model without claiming that it is already used compositionally?

3

Intervention

What changes after an explicit trainable projection/readout is added while the backbone remains frozen?

4

True group position

Does recovery track an opaque algebraic-position target beyond a correlated category label, under shuffled-label controls?

5

Composition

Does the recovered representation support the specified operation on combinations never seen during training?

02 / frozen baselines

Frozen models show strong surface capture and weak target recovery in the adversarial setup.

The dedicated Track D record reports Mistral 7B ARI −0.0337 and Llama 3 8B ARI 0.0152 against the designed orbit/axis labels under its Semantic Starvation protocol. The later Morphological Hijacking series broadens the frozen-baseline framing across GPT2-small, Pythia-410m, Mistral-7B-v0.3 and Qwen2.5-7B, with surface-prefix structure dominating the adversarial Core-30 task.

Boundary: this is a frozen/unremediated result under a deliberately adversarial construction. It is not a universal statement that language models cannot encode algebraic or structural variables.

03 / trained remediation

Explicit training changes the result—and the claim.

The projection-head series trains a lightweight readout using supervised contrastive learning, hard negatives, symmetry regularization, rogue-dimension ablation and Soft-PCA initialization while keeping the backbone frozen. Under model-specific tuning, the reported trained stress-test ARI reaches approximately 0.957 for Mistral-7B and 0.880 for Qwen2.5-7B.

Supported

  • Targeted intervention can substantially improve recovery of the specified structural target.
  • Continuous geometry metrics move consistently with the clustering improvements in the reported experiments.
  • The 300-word Appendix E variant reports pooled held-out-root ARI 0.992 ± 0.007 in its easier same-script/same-order condition.

Not implied

  • Spontaneous semantic discovery by the frozen backbone.
  • A single architecture-independent hyperparameter recipe.
  • Natural-language semantic understanding.
  • Systematic composition.
04 / algebraic-position control

The harder Appendix F target is true group position, not just category labels.

The corrected benchmark uses 5 roots × 6 prefixes × 12 positions = 360 words with opaque suffixes and a shuffled-label control. Reported true-label ARI values are approximately 0.791 ± 0.105 for GPT2-small, 0.929 ± 0.047 for Mistral-7B and 0.996 ± 0.004 for Qwen2.5-7B; shuffled-label controls remain much lower.

Why this matters: it is stronger evidence for targeted recovery of the designed group-position variable than a correlated category label. It still does not test closure, homomorphism, or systematic composition.

05 / composition

The latest composition evidence is negative under the tested procedures.

v3

Morphological Hijacking composition pilot

A capacity-controlled MLP fits seen pairs at about 0.996, then falls to TRUE 0.106 on held-out pairs, below SHUFFLED 0.281 and WRONG_OP 0.175. The diagnostic chain tests optimization, conditioning/rank, operand alignment and decoder capacity before retaining the negative generalization result.

V2

Frozen Qwen Phase 0–2 experiment

The frozen Qwen2.5-1.5B structural variable is highly linearly decodable (surface-span mean BA 0.9666; 25/29 indices at 1.000), yet the preregistered composition phase returns 0/58 PASS, 0/58 AMBIGUOUS, 58/58 FAIL.

Current methodological takeaway: strong decodability or targeted recovery should not, by itself, be treated as evidence that the same representation is a computational substrate for systematic compositional generalization.

06 / reproducibility

The public code archives preserve the diagnostic chain.

The verified v3 Zenodo ZIP contains 40 entries, including scripts 01–25 and the paper source/figures. It includes the arbitrary-scale LUXVAR generator, the 300-word experiment, the intentionally preserved rejected leaking position design, the corrected true-position benchmark with shuffled control, and the composition diagnostic sequence. VARZIN V2 separately exposes the final PDF and the large All code Phase.zip package with the frozen dataset/hashes and Phase 0–2 materials.

07 / historical interpretation

Older positive wording is preserved, but no longer controls the current claim.

The LUXVAR v2.2 title retains “AI-Recoverable Morpheme Families” for citation continuity. Its corrected manuscript and later audits separate inter-model morphemic/surface agreement from recovery of the intended semantic axes. The old 0.812 inter-model figure is therefore historical context, not the headline current evidence.
